mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary cycle, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive (>0%) despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises but S&P 500 returns remain positive over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail and food services sales signals strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Retail sales increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth exceeds 0.5% but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate coupled with a decline in payroll employment indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises and payroll employment declines but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate remains low but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase by more than 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP coupled with a decline in CPI indicates stagflation, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDP increases and CPI declines but S&P 500 returns remain positive.
